messages.body_plain:
Hi Mike,

I have reinstalled the "terra" and "sf" packages, but there are still some errors on the micro_era5(). From the errors, is there an error on the timezone?

Here is the code for micro_era5():

lon=120.98
lat=38.95
year=2018
dstart="01/09/2018"
dfinish="30/09/2018"

lon_min<-floor(lon/5)*5 #the starting longitude of corresponding section
                        #(we divided the earth by every 5 degrees in longitude)
spatial=paste0("/home/2/era5_singlelevel/",year,"/",lon_min,"_",lon_min+5)

#run microclimate model
micro<-try(micro_era5(#Type in parameters that are not default
                      spatial = spatial,
                      loc = c(lon,lat),
                      dstart = dstart,
                      dfinish = dfinish))

And the error results are as follows:

If program is crashing, try run.gads = 2. Authorization required, but no authorization protocol specified Authorization required, but no authorization protocol specified Attaching package: ‘microclima’ The following objects are masked from ‘package:mcera5’: clearskyrad, julday, siflat, solalt, solartime, windheight downloading DEM via package elevatr Registered S3 method overwritten by 'httr': method from print.cache_info hoardr Accessing raster elevation [=========================] 100% Mosaicing & Projecting Note: Elevation units are in meters. extracting weather data locally from /home/2/era5_singlelevel/2018/120_125 Distance weighting applied. Diurnal temperature range correction applied. Some or all dates using system timezone are in CST 5: PROJ support is provided by the sf and terra packages among others 6: PROJ support is provided by the sf and terra packages among others

Your help would be most appreciated!

Best,
Bingbing Liu

messages.body_plain:
Hi Bingbing Liu,

They are all just warnings and none are of concern re the calculations.

This one: Authorization required, but no authorization protocol specified
is nothing to do with NicheMapR and a quick google suggests it's due to you running as root
This one: The following objects are masked from ‘package:mcera5’: clearskyrad, julday, siflat, solalt, solartime, windheight
is due to two packages having the same names for objects and this one: Registered S3 method overwritten by 'httr': method from print.cache_info hoardr
is I think because of packages having common function names
This one: Warning messages: 1: In fun(libname, pkgname) : couldn't connect to display ":0"
is something specific to your system
This one: PROJ support is provided by the sf and terra packages among others
looks like there's something still lingering from the retirement of rgdal but it won't be causing you issues
and this one:  In microclima::microclimaforNMR(lat = longlat[2], long = longlat[1], : Data sequence in UTC/GMT. Some or all dates using system timezone are in CST
is just to warn you to be careful about which time zone you've got for your dates when you're comparing things.

Note however that I found an issue with micro_ncep and micro_era5 to do with time zones that will sometimes result in an error because the rainhr vector isn't constructed properly. It's fixed now in the latest version on github and I'll update the release shortly.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: issue in endoR with dorsal/ventral fur differences
messages.subject_clean: issue in endoR with dorsal/ventral fur differences
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
I just spotted an issue in endoR which becomes apparent when you have different fur properties dorsally and ventrally. It resulted in the program using the mean of dorsal and ventral rather than explicitly using dorsal for the part of the organism facing up and ventral for the part facing down. It's fixed in the latest push to github.
All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: Scenario change
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dave,

Thank you for the reply! This made the issues at hand very clear.

I have since successfully downloaded 2 lots of 6 months (January - June and July - December) for my spatial extent, then combined the two NC files together to represent the full year, as suggested.

Using the combined NC file, the ectotherm model successfully ran with and without the scenario change function (as suggested by Mike earlier in this thread). The original error regarding minshades and maxshades never occurred when using the scenario function with the combined 'full year' NC file.

Everything seems to be working fine!

Thank you both for your help and insight,

Shane

On Friday, May 31, 2024 at 2:38:57 PM UTC+1 dkli...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi Shane,
>
> Thanks for bringing this to my attention. I was surprised you were facing this error about your request having too many fields: for years the limit for ERA5 has been 120,000 fields, and yet your error says the limit is 60,000. A 120,000 for ERA5 hourly single levels is still what the ECMWF documentation Confluence says (see Table 2 here <https://confluence.ecmwf.int/display/CKB/Climate+Data+Store+%28CDS%29+documentation#heading-DatahostedontheCDSMARSinternal>).
>
> But after some digging, I see that in a blog post, the limit for ERA5 just changed from 120,000 to 60,000 in early April, albeit this change should only be temporary:
> https://forum.ecmwf.int/t/a-new-cds-soon-to-be-launched-expect-some-disruptions/1607
>
> As for why the number of fields (105120) may have remained the same even though you shrank the spatial extent: given the large grid cell size of ERA5 (0.25 x 0.25), and the rounding of grid coordinates that request_era5() does under the hood, you sometimes need to decrease the extent considerably in order to change the number of fields. But, it's changing the temporal duration that really does any good in changing # of fields: 12 ERA5 variables x 8,760 hourly timesteps = many fields that stack up over time.
>
> So the request you outline above should work in its entirety, but for the time being you'll need to be flexible with the temporary lower field limit. But regardless, as we suggest in our mcera5 paper <https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/2041-210X.13877>, and also stated in that blog post, the CDS requests will indeed be much more efficient if you request a shorter temporal duration, as Shane did here, and then combine the netCDF files together. Seeing this (albeit temporary) lower limit of 60,000, I might change the combine = TRUE feature in `request_era5()` so that it's easier to combine months rather than just years...will work on this soon!
>
> Cheers,
> Dave
